Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
The test `testEndMb` in the `CaverphoneTest` class is checking the encodings of strings starting and ending with "mb". The test is supposed to encode names ending with "mb" as "m2", but the bug report states that names starting with "mb" are incorrectly encoded as "m2".

Next, I will inspect the `checkEncodings` method to understand how the encoding logic is implemented.

messages.name: get_code_snippet

messages.content:
The `checkEncodings` method in the `StringEncoderAbstractTest` class iterates over a given array of data and calls `checkEncoding` method for each element. 

I will now check the `checkEncoding` method to understand the encoding logic in detail.

messages.name: get_code_snippet
messages.content: "37 :     public void checkEncoding(String expected, String source) throws EncoderException {\n38 :         Assert.assertEquals(\"Source: \" + source, expected, this.getStringEncoder().encode(source));\n39 :     }"

The `checkEncoding` method in the `StringEncoderAbstractTest` class compares the encoded result of a source string with the expected encoded string using `Assert.assertEquals`.

It appears that the issue might be related to the encoding logic within the `getStringEncoder().encode(source)` call. The bug report mentions that names starting with "mb" are incorrectly encoded as "m2" instead of names ending with "mb".

To fix the issue, you may need to revisit the encoding logic in the `getStringEncoder` method of the Caverphone implementation to ensure that names ending with "mb" are encoded as "m2" as specified in the Caverphone spec.

Do you need any more information or assistance with this diagnosis?
